doctrine: What a null costs is a rate, never a total. A total is computed against a task count, and the task count expires the moment new problems are authored; seconds per task does not. The rule this record exists to enforce is the one its own predecessor broke: a constant measured on some cells may not be applied to cells it was not measured on. That is the same defect as a reproducibility bound keyed on everything but its own denominator (ADR-0027 D9).
unit: seconds per task per run, summed from the runner-recorded latency_s (generation) and acceptance_s (gate) of every greedy row
formula: minutes = 2 * n * total_s / 60. A null is a pair, so the dispatched work is 2n tasks.
bound: Summed task time. It excludes harness overhead, model load and the gap between the two runs of a pair, so every figure is a LOWER BOUND on rig occupancy rather than an estimate of it. #289's acceptance requires the overhead term calibrated against r1's session clock before the card is quoted as occupancy.
what_it_replaces: reproducibility.json's matching prose read 'a null costs about 40 minutes to re-measure'. Against the cells below that constant is 2.5x too high for the cheapest and 18% too low for the dearest — a 3.0x spread.
why_two_axes: Generation scales with the model and the gate does not. The gate is 0.20 s/task at BOTH models on bench-py, identical to two decimals, which is what a linter blind to the model's output size looks like; on bench-ts it is 24-48% of the cell. A card keyed only on model would mis-price every ts cell, and one pooled average hides the term that separates the arms.
naming: 'tier' here is the language arm — bench-py / bench-ts — matching run.json and identity.BOUND_MATCH. Note that 'arm' in results.jsonl is the DRAW TYPE ('greedy'), and 'tier' in the product ladder is a worker rung. Three senses across two words; this record uses the BOUND_MATCH one and says so rather than adding a fourth (#289).
derivation: uv run --no-sync python tools/bench/ratecard.py — reads the runs each reproducibility.json bound declares, so the card prices exactly the pairs the bounds were measured on and a second list cannot drift from the first. tests/test_bench_ratecard.py re-derives and refuses a stale record.

fields.model: The served model, as the bound declares it.
fields.tier: The language arm the pair ran on.
fields.runs: The two run/tier directories under records/measurements/ the rate is summed over.
fields.rows: Greedy rows counted across both runs of the pair — the denominator of every rate here.
fields.generation_s: Mean latency_s per task per run.
fields.gate_s: Mean acceptance_s per task per run.
fields.total_s: generation_s + gate_s. The rate the formula multiplies.

measured: 2026-08-16, derived from the r1-commissioning nulls of 2026-08-13 and 2026-08-14.
